content/biomes/wetlands/BIOME.toml.text:
schema_version = 1
id = "wetlands"
name = "Wetlands"
short_description = "A hostile expanse of dark pools, reed beds, sinking paths, and abandoned buildings, where prowling creatures make permanent habitation impossible."
description = """
The Wetlands stretch across low, waterlogged country where slow rivers lose their banks and roads gradually disappear beneath the mud. Dark pools lie between reed beds, peat banks, and islands of coarse grass. Scattered willows lean over the water, their exposed roots gripping the banks like knotted fingers. The horizon is broad but often obscured by ground fog, with crooked rooftops and dead trees appearing as isolated silhouettes.

Travel follows raised earth causeways, narrow plank walkways, and channels marked with wooden stakes. Everything sinks eventually. Bridges tilt, fence posts vanish inch by inch, and old stone buildings stand with their doors permanently underwater. Weathered markers still indicate roads that have required a boat for several generations.

The remains of former habitation rot along the waterways. Empty cottages sag on timber stilts, their roofs split and their hearths cold. Torn fishing nets hang from collapsed racks, wicker traps fill with silt, and abandoned boats knock against the remains of their landings. Hostile creatures prowl the reeds and ruined structures; the Wetlands are too inhospitable for anyone to make a home here.

Floodwater exposes old foundations and burial stones, then conceals them again. On still evenings, bell notes carry across the marsh from places where no towers remain. Beneath the rustle of reeds and the drip of water from rotten timber, the empty landscape feels watchful.
"""

[setting]
terrain = "Low, waterlogged ground cut by slow rivers and shallow channels. Dark peat pools, dense reed beds, coarse grass islands, scattered willows, and exposed roots break up the open water. Sinking causeways and damaged plank walkways connect patches of firmer ground; old roads and building entrances disappear below the waterline."
inhabitants = "Hostile creatures prowl the waterways, reed beds, and abandoned structures. Bog Toads lie low along muddy banks and reed-fringed pools. There are no settled residents, working villages, or staffed inns. Cottages, boats, peat workings, and fishing equipment are remnants of former habitation."
supernatural = "Bell notes sometimes carry across still water from places where no towers remain. Floods reveal and conceal old foundations and burial stones, leaving the source of the sound uncertain."
environmental_pressure_and_humor = "Soft ground, concealed water depth, rotten crossings, poor visibility, and prowling enemies make travel dangerous and permanent habitation untenable. Dry humor lies in obsolete practical details: road markers still point confidently into open water, while layers of old repairs sink along with the structures they once supported."

[visual]
lighting = "Soft gray daylight beneath low cloud, with subdued reflections across dark water. Ground fog obscures distant banks and leaves crooked roofs and dead trees as isolated silhouettes. Empty cottages have cold hearths, and the remaining lanterns are unlit. Rust provides a restrained warm accent."
materials = ["dark peat", "slick mud", "waterlogged gray timber", "coarse yellow reeds", "mossy stone", "tarnished iron", "rust", "rotting rope", "frayed netting", "silt-coated wicker", "wet bark"]
weather = "Persistent damp, low cloud, intermittent drizzle, and mist that gathers close to the water, especially toward evening."
ambient_sounds = ["water dripping from rotten timber", "reeds rustling against one another", "distant frogs", "the soft knock of abandoned boats against broken landings", "water lapping at submerged walls", "occasional distant bell notes with no visible source"]
ambient_motion = "Reeds bend in slow gusts, duckweed shifts across shallow pools, loose cloth stirs on channel markers, and half-sunken boats rock against old posts. Thin ground fog drifts between banks and through abandoned buildings."

[[visual.palette]]
name = "Peat brown"
color = "#3E3029"

[[visual.palette]]
name = "Dull olive"
color = "#62684A"

[[visual.palette]]
name = "Reed yellow"
color = "#A29665"

[[visual.palette]]
name = "Weathered timber gray"
color = "#77776B"

[[visual.palette]]
name = "Dark water"
color = "#252F2D"

[[visual.palette]]
name = "Ground fog"
color = "#ADB2A7"

[[visual.palette]]
name = "Muted rust"
color = "#8A543C"

[generation]
composition = "Broad stretches of low water and reeds establish an open, horizontal landscape. Broken walkways and strips of raised earth form the visible travel route, bordered by shallow pools, exposed roots, and flood debris. Scattered willows and abandoned cottages interrupt the middle distance, while fog softens distant rooftops and dead trees. Ruined structures and neglected equipment convey former habitation; there are no active settlements, occupied homes, maintained fishing operations, or welcoming inn lights."

[[sites]]
id = "wetlands_abandoned_stilt_cottages"
name = "Abandoned stilt cottages"
description = "A small cluster of empty timber cottages stands unevenly above the water on rotting stilts and raised foundations. Moss weighs down split roofs; narrow porches sag, and broken ladders descend into the mud. Old repairs overlap beneath newer damage. The interiors are dark, with cold hearths and collapsed floorboards."

[[sites]]
id = "wetlands_disused_peat_workings"
name = "Disused peat workings"
description = "Rectangular cuts in a low bank have filled with dark water. Nearby stacks of peat blocks slump beneath the remnants of patched covers, their once-straight edges softened by rain. Reeds grow through the narrow strips of ground between the flooded cuts."

[[sites]]
id = "wetlands_drowned_masonry"
name = "Drowned masonry"
description = "Half-submerged boundary walls and small stone shrines emerge from shallow pools. Worn steps descend into water that hides their lower ends. Silt collects along exposed ledges, while old foundations and tilted burial stones appear where the water has receded."


# Art targets in logical pixels, independent of device resolution and model settings.
# Every background layer shares this canvas. The hero's feet meet ground_y.
[generation.scene]
canvas = [640, 360]
ground_y = 288
reference_height = 64
view = "orthographic_side"
style = "Pixel art with broad, readable shapes, restrained dark outlines and stepped clusters of muted color. Weathered dark fantasy; wet wood, peat and reeds carry the detail. Distant shapes lose contrast and detail, while foreground shapes remain distinct from the adventurer."
avoid = ["photorealism", "isometric or overhead view", "a road receding toward a vanishing point", "characters or enemies baked into scenery", "occupied cottages", "lit windows or lanterns", "working settlements", "visible bell towers explaining the distant bells", "text or readable lettering", "soft airbrushed edges", "dense high-contrast detail behind combatants"]

# All sections use this edge contract and can be joined in any order.
# surface_y aligns with scene.ground_y; the soil extends to the scene's bottom.
[generation.ground]
canvas = [256, 96]
surface_y = 24
edge_margin = 16
repeat_x = true
edge_description = "The first and last 16 columns share the same level peat-path cross-section: a subdued olive turf lip at row 24, dark compact peat below, and sparse short reed stubble above. The outer edge columns match when repeated. Distinctive boards, roots, stones and puddles stay within the middle 224 columns and taper back to this common edge. There are no open gaps, vertical steps or raised obstacles along the walking surface. Pixels above the turf silhouette are transparent; the soil below it is opaque through the bottom edge."

# Ordered from farthest to nearest. Layers after the sky have transparent space.
# repeat_x describes the intended asset; it does not certify generated seams.

[[background_layers]]
id = "wetlands_overcast_sky"
name = "Low overcast sky"
visual_description = "A low ceiling of gray-green cloud hangs over the marsh. Broad, uneven bands of pale gray gather near the horizon, while the upper sky is a cooler, darker slate. The light is diffuse and there is no distinct sun or bright opening in the cloud."

[background_layers.generation]
parallax = 0.0
repeat_x = true
transparent = false
composition = "Fill the entire 640 by 360 canvas with opaque sky and subdued atmospheric color. Keep cloud masses broad and low contrast, with no trees, buildings, terrain or figures. Match the left and right edges without a border or a conspicuous repeated cloud. Fog is represented by solid bands of stepped color rather than translucent bloom."

[[background_layers]]
id = "wetlands_distant_silhouettes"
name = "Distant drowned treeline"
visual_description = "Thin dead trunks, sparse willow crowns and a few crooked roof ridges emerge from the low mist. Long gaps of open horizon separate the silhouettes. Their gray-green edges merge with the damp air, and neither doors nor individual branches can be distinguished at this distance."

[background_layers.generation]
parallax = 0.15
repeat_x = true
transparent = true
composition = "Use the shared scene canvas, leaving the upper sky transparent. Confine most silhouettes to rows 150 through 250; let low haze-colored bank shapes reach the bottom edge. Use a narrow, low-contrast color range and sparse roofs with no window lights. Leave generous open gaps and compatible left and right edges. Keep near trees, isolated props and the walking path out of this layer."

[[background_layers]]
id = "wetlands_reed_banks"
name = "Pools and middle-distance reed banks"
visual_description = "Long pools of nearly black water separate low peat islands. Dull yellow reeds gather along the banks, interrupted by slick exposed mud, shallow rectangular peat cuts and low fragments of drowned stonework. Narrow gray reflections break across the water beneath the reeds, while the channels remain broad and still."

[background_layers.generation]
parallax = 0.35
repeat_x = true
transparent = true
composition = "Use the shared scene canvas with transparent space above the bank silhouettes. Place the banks and pools mainly below row 220, continuing their color to the bottom behind the separate ground strip. Keep the area above the walking baseline at row 288 quiet enough to read a 64-pixel adventurer. Match water levels, bank colors and silhouettes at the horizontal seam. No nearby willows, cottages, freestanding props or playable path are baked into this layer."

[[ground_sections]]
id = "wetlands_raised_peat_path"
name = "Raised peat causeway"
visual_description = "A narrow crown of firm brown peat runs above the surrounding wet ground. Coarse olive grass grips its ragged edges, and small flattened stones lie pressed into the mud. Darker damp patches and a few shallow puddles interrupt the trodden surface without breaking the route."

[ground_sections.generation]
composition = "A level side-on travel strip with a narrow visible upper lip and an opaque peat face below it. Small puddles are surface markings, not holes. Keep reeds and stones low, retain the shared edge profile, and leave the space above the path clear for feet and combat silhouettes."

[[ground_sections]]
id = "wetlands_plank_walkway"
name = "Uneven plank walkway"
visual_description = "Bowed gray boards rest on posts of unequal height. Mismatched patches show repeated attempts to keep the crossing usable, but several planks have split or fallen away, exposing shallow water and mud below."

[ground_sections.generation]
composition = "A short patched board crossing embedded within the peat causeway. Keep the supported walking surface level at row 24; missing boards reveal mud below without creating a required jump. Show the exposed board ends and a few short supports from the side. Boards begin and end inside the central span, returning to the common peat edge within the 16-column margins."

[[ground_sections]]
id = "wetlands_root_bound_path"
name = "Root-bound peat causeway"
visual_description = "Flattened willow roots thread through a strip of compact peat. Their wet bark is almost black beneath rubbed gray ridges, with small pockets of coarse grass caught between them. Stranded reed blades and patches of mud lie across the roots where repeated floods have passed."

[ground_sections.generation]
composition = "Keep the roots pressed into or immediately beneath the walking surface, with no raised root arch, trunk or obstacle above the route. Let the distinctive root pattern taper out before the shared peat edge margins. Preserve a continuous level silhouette and the opaque soil below it."

content/biomes/wetlands/SCENERY.toml.text:
# Library of eligible visual props, not a scripted route or a spawn order.
# All entries are static transparent cutouts. Scene style, lighting and palette
# come from BIOME.toml. Canvas sizes and relative heights are initial art targets.
# Enemy spawning is independent of this library.
schema_version = 1
biome_id = "wetlands"

[[scenery]]
id = "wetlands_channel_marker"
name = "Channel marker"
visual_description = "A leaning wooden stake carries a faded strip of cloth and a series of carved water-level marks. Its lower half is dark with moisture, and fragments of weed cling around the latest flood line."

[scenery.generation]
canvas = [64, 128]
height_scale = 1.4
layers = ["behind_path"]
anchor = "ground"
composition = "One leaning stake and its attached cloth, fully visible on transparency. The foot is the ground anchor. Carved notches are simple marks, with no lettering; exclude surrounding reeds, water and other stakes."

[[scenery]]
id = "wetlands_obsolete_road_marker"
name = "Obsolete road marker"
visual_description = "A weathered direction board remains firmly attached to a crooked post. Its arrow points along the vanished course of a road, directly into an uninterrupted stretch of dark water."

[scenery.generation]
canvas = [96, 128]
height_scale = 1.5
layers = ["behind_path"]
anchor = "ground"
composition = "One crooked post with an arrow-shaped board, all parts inside the transparent canvas. Keep the direction readable through silhouette alone; no lettering. The post base is the anchor. Its placement beside water can convey the obsolete route without painting water into the prop."

[[scenery]]
id = "wetlands_abandoned_boat"
name = "Abandoned flat-bottomed boat"
visual_description = "A broad, shallow wooden hull sits partly flooded beside a broken landing. Mud streaks its sides; a worn pole, coils of rotting rope, and a battered bailing bucket lie among leaves and standing water inside."

[scenery.generation]
canvas = [192, 96]
height_scale = 0.8
layers = ["behind_path"]
anchor = "waterline"
composition = "A single broadside hull with a small view into its flooded interior. Keep the pole, rope and bucket inside or attached to the boat. The lower hull meets the waterline anchor; no landing, separate water patch, reflection or shore is included."

[[scenery]]
id = "wetlands_wicker_fish_traps"
name = "Discarded wicker traps"
visual_description = "Long eel baskets and rounded fish traps lie tipped against the bank. Their wicker ribs are stained with silt, split at the narrow openings, and threaded with young reeds."

[scenery.generation]
canvas = [96, 64]
height_scale = 0.65
layers = ["behind_path", "foreground"]
anchor = "ground"
composition = "One compact group of two overlapping traps, with a few attached reed blades. Use broad broken ribs that remain readable as pixels; avoid a dense fine mesh. Keep the ground and water transparent around the group."

[[scenery]]
id = "wetlands_collapsed_net_rack"
name = "Collapsed net rack"
visual_description = "Torn fishing nets hang in heavy folds from a wooden rack with one broken upright. Frayed mesh trails into the water, holding leaves, twigs, and patches of green growth."

[scenery.generation]
canvas = [128, 128]
height_scale = 1.5
layers = ["behind_path"]
anchor = "ground"
composition = "The broken rack and its hanging net form one complete isolated prop. Simplify frayed mesh into a few connected bands and conspicuous holes. Include the foot of the remaining upright as the ground anchor, with no painted pool or bank."

[[scenery]]
id = "wetlands_unlit_lantern"
name = "Abandoned lantern"
visual_description = "A small iron lantern hangs beneath a decaying eave or beside an empty landing. Rust gathers around the hinges, cloudy glass obscures its empty interior, and one cracked pane admits damp air. No flame burns inside."

[scenery.generation]
canvas = [64, 96]
height_scale = 0.95
layers = ["behind_path"]
anchor = "ground"
composition = "Keep the unlit lantern attached to a short rotten landing post with a bent iron bracket. Include the entire post down to its ground anchor so this prop can stand independently. The glass has dull solid highlights; there is no flame, glow or surrounding landing."

[[scenery]]
id = "wetlands_reed_clump"
name = "Reeds and rushes"
visual_description = "Dense stems of dull olive and straw yellow grow along the margins of pools. Bent stalks cross above the water, and dead blades collect in tangled mats around their bases."

[scenery.generation]
canvas = [96, 96]
height_scale = 0.9
layers = ["behind_path", "foreground"]
anchor = "ground"
composition = "One irregular clump with a clear base and a few thick, bent stalks. Preserve open gaps using hard transparency and keep tips inside the canvas. No water rectangle or ground patch surrounds it. Foreground placement stays at the lower edge of the scene."

[[scenery]]
id = "wetlands_duckweed"
name = "Drifting duckweed"
visual_description = "Small muted green leaves gather in irregular rafts across sheltered water. Narrow black gaps and curved breaks interrupt the surface where water moves around posts and roots."

[scenery.generation]
canvas = [96, 32]
height_scale = 0.2
layers = ["behind_path"]
anchor = "waterline"
composition = "A low raft seen at the same shallow side-view angle as the scene pools. Use simple connected leaf clusters separated by transparent gaps. Do not include black water, reflections or a square backing; the raft rests on the waterline anchor."

[[scenery]]
id = "wetlands_willow_roots"
name = "Exposed willow roots"
visual_description = "Thick, knotted roots grip an eroded peat bank beneath a leaning willow. Wet bark darkens their undersides, while coarse grass and stranded reeds catch in the spaces between them."

[scenery.generation]
canvas = [128, 64]
height_scale = 0.65
layers = ["behind_path", "foreground"]
anchor = "ground"
composition = "One low cluster of roots, with a short broken trunk base to explain their attachment. No full tree or separate peat-bank rectangle. Keep the broad root contacts at the ground anchor and all openings transparent. Foreground placement remains below the combat silhouettes."

[[scenery]]
id = "wetlands_shelf_fungi"
name = "Pale shelf fungi"
visual_description = "Small cream and gray fungal shelves crowd the shaded sides of rotten posts and fallen branches. Their layered edges stand out against dark, saturated wood."

[scenery.generation]
canvas = [64, 64]
height_scale = 0.45
layers = ["behind_path", "foreground"]
anchor = "ground"
composition = "The pale shelves stay attached to one short rotten stump. Include its base as the ground anchor; do not produce floating fungi. Group the shelves into a few readable tiers, without luminous edges or a separate ground patch."

[[scenery]]
id = "wetlands_flood_debris"
name = "Flood debris"
visual_description = "Branches, broken fence rails, and scraps of faded fabric lodge against roots and supports above the current waterline. Mud coats the lower pieces, marking the height of an earlier flood."

[scenery.generation]
canvas = [128, 64]
height_scale = 0.55
layers = ["behind_path", "foreground"]
anchor = "ground"
composition = "A low tangle caught against a single broken support. Keep branches, rails and fabric connected or overlapping as one isolated prop. Leave irregular holes transparent and exclude a surrounding bank. Foreground placement stays below the walking silhouettes."

[[scenery]]
id = "wetlands_sinking_fence"
name = "Sinking fence remnants"
visual_description = "A short run of crooked posts emerges from coarse grass and shallow water. A few warped rails remain attached, descending toward the mud until the final section disappears beneath it."

[scenery.generation]
canvas = [192, 96]
height_scale = 0.95
layers = ["behind_path"]
anchor = "ground"
composition = "A short, complete span of three uneven posts and warped attached rails. Let the last rail descend to the anchor level without painting a water or mud rectangle around it. Keep both ends fully visible; this is an isolated prop, not a repeating fence tile."

[[scenery]]
id = "wetlands_leaning_willow"
name = "Leaning marsh willow"
visual_description = "A thick willow trunk leans beneath an uneven crown of dull olive leaves. Long, sparse branchlets droop around open gaps in the foliage, their tips browned and ragged. Deep grooves split the wet gray bark, and broad exposed roots spread from the swollen base with dead reeds caught between them."

[scenery.generation]
canvas = [192, 256]
height_scale = 3.4
layers = ["behind_path"]
anchor = "ground"
composition = "One complete side-view tree with its crown, hanging branchlets and root base inside the transparent canvas. Use broad leaf clusters and a few substantial hanging strands instead of hair-thin twigs. The root contacts form the ground anchor. Keep open gaps in the canopy; no pool, sky, cast-shadow patch or other trees."

[[scenery]]
id = "wetlands_dead_willow"
name = "Dead marsh willow"
visual_description = "A hollow gray trunk rises from a splayed root base and divides into a few crooked limbs. The upper branches end in pale broken stubs, while a single long branch bends downward under its own weight. Dark cavities interrupt the flaking bark, and scraps of floodweed cling near the swollen roots."

[scenery.generation]
canvas = [128, 256]
height_scale = 3.0
layers = ["behind_path"]
anchor = "ground"
composition = "A complete isolated tree with thick readable branches, open transparent gaps and a visible root anchor. Keep the silhouette asymmetrical and the snapped tips inside the canvas. No face, moving limbs, leaves or surrounding water."

[[scenery]]
id = "wetlands_ruined_stilt_cottage"
name = "Ruined stilt cottage"
visual_description = "An empty timber cottage sags above a row of uneven, rotting stilts. Its low roof carries heavy patches of moss and a long split through the shingles. A narrow porch tilts away from the dark doorway, and a broken ladder hangs from one end. Overlapping repair boards cover old damage, but gaps in the wall reveal an unlit, abandoned interior."

[scenery.generation]
canvas = [256, 192]
height_scale = 2.3
layers = ["behind_path"]
anchor = "ground"
composition = "One small cottage seen broadside with a slight view under the eaves, consistent with the orthographic scene. Include all stilts and the broken ladder as attached parts. Stilt bottoms define the ground anchor. Leave gaps between supports transparent; no water, sky, smoke, figures or lit windows."

[[scenery]]
id = "wetlands_slumped_peat_stack"
name = "Slumped peat stack"
visual_description = "A squat stack of dark peat blocks has slumped into irregular layers. A torn gray cover hangs over one side, held down by a mossy stone. Rain has rounded the edges of the blocks, and small reeds grow through the gaps at the base."

[scenery.generation]
canvas = [96, 64]
height_scale = 0.65
layers = ["behind_path", "foreground"]
anchor = "ground"
composition = "One low stack with its attached cover, stone and reed shoots. Keep the silhouette compact and the spaces around it transparent. No cutting tools, workers, peat pit or surrounding bank. Foreground placement stays low in the scene."

[[scenery]]
id = "wetlands_drowned_wall"
name = "Drowned stone wall"
visual_description = "A short remnant of rough gray masonry stands unevenly above its stained lower courses. One end has collapsed into a few large blocks, while the other retains a shallow corner and a worn step. Moss fills the joints, and a dark silt line crosses the exposed stones near the base."

[scenery.generation]
canvas = [192, 96]
height_scale = 1.0
layers = ["behind_path"]
anchor = "waterline"
composition = "A single low wall fragment with attached fallen blocks and step, seen from the side. The silt line near the base identifies the waterline anchor. Exclude water, reflections, buildings and the rest of the ruin; preserve clear gaps between the upper broken stones."

scene.style: Pixel art with broad, readable shapes, restrained dark outlines and stepped clusters of muted color. Weathered dark fantasy; wet wood, peat and reeds carry the detail. Distant shapes lose contrast and detail, while foreground shapes remain distinct from the adventurer.
avoid: a road receding toward a vanishing point
characters or enemies baked into scenery
visible bell towers explaining the distant bells

The outer edge columns match when repeated. Distinctive boards, roots, stones and puddles stay within the middle 224 columns and taper back to this common edge. There are no open gaps, vertical steps or raised obstacles along the walking surface. Pixels above the turf silhouette are transparent; the soil below it is opaque through the bottom edge.

source.name: Leaning marsh willow
source.visual_description: A thick willow trunk leans beneath an uneven crown of dull olive leaves. Long, sparse branchlets droop around open gaps in the foliage, their tips browned and ragged. Deep grooves split the wet gray bark, and broad exposed roots spread from the swollen base with dead reeds caught between them.
